text:
maya: FYI CI microbench flagged PR #6123 — kv_cache hitrate down ~18% vs base after the quantization-heuristic change. Canary blocked. https://git/repo/pull/6123 :eyes:
ci-bot: microbench-suite: kv_cache_hitrate@p50 dropped from 0.72 -> 0.59 (diff -0.13, -18.1%)
ci-bot: failing test: runtime/microbench/kv_cache_hitrate.test — threshold -0.05 exceeded
pranav: ugh. which commit in the PR touched kernel selection vs quant heuristics?
zach: PR edits runtime/kernel_selector.cc + quant/heuristics.py — primary change is introducing "quant_cost_adjustment" that biases against slower kernels for quantized ops
sophie: I pulled a flamegraph from the perf run (short):
```
  kv_lookup (hot)  48%\n  attention_kv_cache  35%\n  kernel_dispatch  12%\n  memcpy  5%\n```
sophie: looks like more time in kv_lookup and less in kernel_dispatch; weird — suggests we lost an optimized kernel path and are doing more python-level kv bookkeeping
maya: can someone run a targeted microbench local with PR head vs base? Suggest command:
```
tools/run_local_bench --suite kv_cache_hitrate --runs 5 --release_tier canary --commit HEAD~0 --compare base
```
pranav: running now, will post results in ~5m :thumbsup:
pranav: (results) head: 0.59, base: 0.71, stdev small — reproduces locally
pranav: profiling diff attached: more calls into kernel_selector::choose_kernel_for_op, but chosen kernel falls back to generic_quantized_impl which has worse KV prefetch behavior
zach: that matches my suspicion — the cost model's overhead estimate now punishes certain fused kernels which previously handled KV prefetching inline. The quant adjustment added a flat penalty that didn't account for KV hit patterns
sophie: here's a short snippet from the selector that changed:
```
if (op.is_quantized()) {
  score += quant_cost_adjustment; // previously 0
}
```
sophie: quant_cost_adjustment is +0.04 for all ops in the PR
maya: +0.04 across the board sounds risky. Can we make it dependent on op type or kv-friendly flag?
zach: quick mitigation: reduce quant_cost_adjustment to +0.0 for attention and kv-related ops, or compute it as a function of kv_prefetch_score
pranav: I tried a quick patch reverting the quant_cost_adjustment for kv ops locally and re-ran microbench: head (patched) -> 0.70, base 0.71 — diff now within threshold
pranav: patch diff:
```
- if (op.is_quantized()) score += quant_cost_adjustment;
+ if (op.is_quantized() && !op.has_kv_prefetch()) score += quant_cost_adjustment;
```
maya: nice. two options: 1) revert the PR until a proper fix, 2) land a targeted patch to skip the penalty for kv ops and re-run canary. Any preference?
zach: for safety revert PR 6123 asap, then re-land smaller patch after tests. PR has multiple changes beyond the quant tweak so safer to revert quickly
pranav: I can open a revert PR now and request fast-track.
maya: do it. ping @oncall if rollout is blocked by canary guard
pranav: opened revert: https://git/repo/pull/6130 — reverting quant heuristic changes from #6123 — request review from @zach @sophie
pranav: also queued a targeted patch branch with the conditional skip — will add tests for kv ops
oncall-bot: Alert escalated to oncall: canary failed for microperf threshold. Revert PR 6130 created.
maya: thanks everyone. postmortem action: add microbench unit that exercises op.has_kv_prefetch() paths and add cost-model tests. I'll create a ticket.
